title: Emberglow - Private Connectivity Discovery and Region Constraints
summary: Intro call to understand Emberglow's private/VPC onramp needs: region exclusions, private endpoints vs peering, egress IP constraints, and security requirements (SOC2/SAML/KMS). Agreed to run a short connectivity test and share security pack and pricing banding. Next steps: SE-run latency/bandwidth test, security questionnaire, follow-up with demo environment access.
action_items: Marcus Chen (Redwood SE): provide list of private endpoint FQDNs and sample TLS fingerprint for firewall rules (due 2026-07-23)
Lena Park (Redwood AE): send draft pricing tiers and Dedicated vs Private gating doc (due 2026-07-22)
Tom Nguyen (Emberglow): return completed security questionnaire and preferred region list (due 2026-07-24)
next_steps: Schedule SE-led connectivity test (Marcus to propose times)
Share security pack + SOC2 report link
Provision short-lived demo tenant with private endpoint for PoC
Follow-up call next week to review test results and finalize pilot scope
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-19
Time: 08:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Jared Cole (Emberglow - Head of Infra), Maya Alvarez (Emberglow - Security), Tom Nguyen (Emberglow - Cloud Eng)

Auto-generated summary: intro & high-level ask present, see notes below (auto-summary may omit some details)

[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm lena with Redwood Inference, i'll run the intro, quick intro from you all?
[00:12] Jared Cole: hey lena, Jared here, i run infra at emberglow. we build a vector search and model orchestration stack, looking at private deployment options for inference due to regulatory clients.
[00:22] Maya Alvarez: maya, security lead, mostly to cover compliance and audit needs.
[00:28] Tom Nguyen: tom, cloud eng, i'll handle network and firewall questions.
[00:34] Lena Park: great, and with me is marcus chen our se, he'll take the deep network Qs. quick agenda: understand current network topology, region restrictions, acceptable connectivity patterns (peering vs priv endpoints), egress ip constraints, and next steps for a PoC. sound good?
[00:48] Group: yes / yup / yep

-- Discovery and qualification --
[01:05] Marcus Chen: quick q to start — are you leaning hosted/dedicated/private or is this strictly private/VPC onramp?
[01:14] Jared Cole: primary ask is private - emberglow needs inference inside our VPC for certain customers. we may evaluate dedicated later but must satisfy private VPC peering or priv endpoint model first.
[01:28] Marcus Chen: understood. how many regions do you need? any region exclusions?
[01:32] Tom Nguyen: we run prod in us-west-2 and eu-west-1, but we have a contract requiring no data crossing into apac for one vertical. so apac must be blocked and we need region gating.
[01:46] Maya Alvarez: and we need to maintain audit logs + be able to map tokens to tenant ids for compliance - retention policy is 90 days for logs.
[01:56] Lena Park: perfect, region gating is supported — we can pin model endpoints to specific regions and block fallback, but we'll need to document that and agree on routing policy. we'll also surface audit logs, pointing to console retention settings.

[02:15] Marcus Chen: on connectivity pattern — we support two main flows: VPC peering/transit gateway style (our pods sit in a customer peered VPC) or private endpoints (privatelink-style). Each has tradeoffs: peering gives direct L3 access and lower latency for high throughput; private endpoints reduce blast radius and are easier with strict routing but add NAT/egress translation.
[02:49] Tom Nguyen: with peering, do you need route table updates or do you do proxying?
[02:54] Marcus Chen: we typically ask customers to peer to our service VPC; however for private deployment (private control plane) we can place inference nodes inside your VPC if you take an on-prem bundle. For hosted-private, we do priv endpoints and you route to them — that tends to be easiest for segmented networks.
[03:12] Jared Cole: latency is a factor — sub 100ms p95 is our bar for interactive features. if priv endpoints add too much egress hops we might hit it.
[03:22] Marcus Chen: totally, for conversational workloads p95 under 100ms is doable with peering and colocated regions; priv endpoints usually add 5-30ms depending on transit. we can run a latency test from your VPC to our endpoint during PoC.

-- Security and compliance --
[03:45] Maya Alvarez: security checklist: SOC2 type II available? SAML SSO? RBAC? KMS integration for customer keys? audit logs?
[03:55] Lena Park: yes we have SOC2 reports; sso via SAML/okta supported, RBAC for console and tokens, and KMS integrations for BYOK/HSM for Private deployments. we'll share the security pack link after the call.
[04:10] Maya Alvarez: for BYOK, is it customer-managed keys in cloud KMS or do you offer HSM connectors?
[04:16] Marcus Chen: we support both: cloud KMS (AWS KMS) integration for hosted/private and HSM connectors for air-gapped/on-prem installs. for the private onprem bundle, keys never leave your HSM.
[04:26] Maya Alvarez: good. audit trail detail—can we export raw event logs?
[04:30] Lena Park: yes, full audit events are exportable to s3 or your SIEM via streaming. retention can be configured but note hosted default is 30 days without add-on.

-- Network specifics and egress --
[04:44] Tom Nguyen: real quick on egress IPs — we have perimeter firewalls that require a static egress IP list. can you provide a stable set of IPs for private endpoints or peered subnets?
[04:54] Marcus Chen: for dedicated pools we can provide static egress IPs; for shared hosted it's more dynamic. For priv endpoints you typically open FQDNs and allow TLS SNI, or we can supply static NAT IPs if you use a dedicated NAT gateway in our private setup. i'll follow up with the exact IP ranges.
[05:13] Tom Nguyen: we prefer IPs (firewall rules), FQDNs are harder for us.
[05:18] Marcus Chen: noted — action: i'll list IP ranges and any expected port/protocols.

[05:30] Jared Cole: what about kv cache or long-running sessions — session affinity?
[05:36] Marcus Chen: we maintain KV cache per model session; in peered deployments you have direct access to the cache nodes; in private endpoint style we manage the cache and expose stable connections — there may be small serialization overhead, but functionally the same. sometimes transcripters call it K-V catch or K-V cash, so docs will clarify.

-- Deep dive: peering vs priv endpoints (customer questions) --
[06:05] Tom Nguyen: if we go with peering and transit gateway, how do we handle cross-account IAM and security groups?
[06:12] Marcus Chen: you can peer cross-account or use an interface VPC endpoint. Security groups are enforced on our side for inbound. For cross-account we provide an ARN-based role to allow limited provisioning if you want infrastructure automation.
[06:28] Maya Alvarez: encryption in transit? at-rest?
[06:31] Lena Park: all traffic TLS1.2+ in transit; at rest we encrypt via KMS and can bring your own keys for private deployments.

-- PoC and timeline --
[06:48] Jared Cole: timeline: we want to start a 4-week PoC in early august. core success criteria: sub 100ms p95 within our eu-west-1 region, ability to pin endpoints to region, and delivering SOC2 artifacts and a KMS/BYOK plan.
[07:05] Lena Park: sounds reasonable. we can provision a demo tenant and run a 1-day connectivity test followed by a week-long throughput run.
[07:12] Marcus Chen: i'll coordinate test harness: a small load generator inside your VPC hitting the private endpoint or peered endpoint depending on chosen flow. we'll include raw latency + token cost breakdowns.

-- Misc and clarifications --
[07:30] Tom Nguyen: ports — what's needed?
[07:33] Marcus Chen: outbound 443 for priv endpoints; for peering we need your CIDR block routes to our service subnet(s) and allow ephemeral ports for TLS flow. i'll add specifics in follow-up doc.
[07:47] Maya Alvarez: data residency — if a request from eu-west-1 is processed in us-west-2, not allowed. how do you prevent cross-region failover?
[07:58] Lena Park: we can configure routing policies and pin model deployments to region. automatic fallback to another region is opt-in — by default for these contracts we disable cross-region fallback. we'll capture this in the SLA addendum.

[08:18] Marcus Chen: one caveat — if you ask for pinned region and also ask for dedicated capacity, we may need minimum committed throughput (GPU reservation) to guarantee latency SLOs. we'll outline commit tiers.
[08:32] Jared Cole: okay, budget side — rough pricing bands for private onramp vs dedicated?
[08:37] Lena Park: i'll send the high-level bands after this call. dedicated is higher but gives fixed egress IPs and guaranteed throughput. private with priv endpoints is mid tier and easier to start.

-- Questions from customer --
[08:50] Tom Nguyen: can we do mTLS to your endpoints?
[08:53] Marcus Chen: we support mTLS for private deployments; for hosted private endpoints TLS with SNI is the default but mTLS is available for an enterprise add-on.
[08:59] Maya Alvarez: request for SOC2 and penetration test summary — can you share the last report?
[09:04] Lena Park: yes will send redacted SOC2 and pen test summary link (drive link: https://drive.google.com/reds/security-pack-placeholder).

-- Closing & recap --
[09:20] Lena Park: recap: 1) Marcus to share IP ranges, endpoint FQDNs, and port list and propose connectivity test times. 2) Lena will send pricing bands and SOC2/security pack. 3) Emberglow to return security questionnaire and preferred regions. 4) schedule PoC connectivity test next week.
[09:40] Jared Cole: sounds good, appreciate it.
[09:44] Maya Alvarez: thanks everyone, will review and send back questionnaire.
[09:48] Tom Nguyen: i'll try to carve out a time for the connectivity test, prefer m-f mornings.
[09:52] Lena Park: great, we'll follow up with a calendar invite and the docs. thanks all.

Notes: transcription contains occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., "K-V catch" in place of KV cache, some names mis-attributed by auto-transcriber). Links and artifacts referenced: security-pack (drive google link), pricing spreadsheet (redwood-pricing-link placeholder), PoC test harness doc (internal link).
